name: BQ25570RGRR
title: Nano-power boost charger with MPPT and buck converter for energy harvesting
summary: The bq25570 takes power from a high-impedance DC harvester such as a solar cell or thermoelectric generator and boosts it into a rechargeable cell, supercapacitor or capacitor, holding the source at a sampled maximum power point. It cold-starts from 600 mV and keeps harvesting down to 100 mV, protects the storage element with a fixed undervoltage cut-off and a resistor-set overvoltage limit, and flags a programmable battery-good level. A nano-power buck converter supplies a resistor-set rail of up to about 110 mA. It draws 488 nA in full operation and comes in a 3.5 mm × 3.5 mm 20-pin VQFN.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Power ground of the boost charger.

pins.name: VIN_DC
pins.function: DC input from the harvester. Takes at least 4.7 µF to pin 1, placed tight against the pins; L1 joins it to LBOOST.

pins.name: VOC_SAMP
pins.function: MPPT sampling input. Tie to VSTOR for 80 % of the source's open-circuit voltage, to GND for 50 %, or to the tap of a divider from VIN_DC to GND for another fraction.

pins.name: VREF_SAMP
pins.function: Holds the sampled MPPT voltage that VIN_DC is regulated to, on a 0.01 µF low-leakage capacitor to GND.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Active-low enable for the whole IC; tie to GND to keep it on. High (relative to VBAT) puts the IC in ship mode.

pins.name: VOUT_EN
pins.function: Active-high enable for the buck converter; tie to VSTOR to keep the buck on.

pins.name: VBAT_OV
pins.function: Tap of the divider from VRDIV to GND that sets the battery overvoltage threshold.

pins.name: VRDIV
pins.function: Bias output that feeds the top of every threshold-setting divider.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Ties to ground through the IC's PowerPAD.

pins.name: OK_HYST
pins.function: Tap of a divider from VRDIV to GND setting the rising VBAT_OK threshold; GND when unused.

pins.name: OK_PROG
pins.function: Tap of a divider from VRDIV to GND setting the falling VBAT_OK threshold; GND when unused.

pins.name: VOUT_SET
pins.function: Tap of the divider from VRDIV to GND that sets the buck output voltage.

pins.name: VBAT_OK
pins.function: Battery-good logic output, its high level taken from VSTOR. Leave open when unused.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.function: Buck output; at least 22 µF to pin 15, and L2 from LBUCK.

pins.name: VSS
pins.function: Buck power ground, and the quiet return for the divider resistors and the VREF_SAMP capacitor.

pins.name: LBUCK
pins.function: Buck switching node; an inductor of 4.7 µH or more joins it to VOUT.

pins.name: NC
pins.function: Ties to ground through the IC's PowerPAD.

pins.name: VBAT
pins.function: Storage element connection: a rechargeable cell or capacitor of at least 100 µF equivalent, returned to a VSS pin.

pins.name: VSTOR
pins.function: Boost charger output and system supply node. Takes at least 4.7 µF in parallel with 0.1 µF to pin 1, close to the pins.

pins.name: LBOOST
pins.function: Boost switching node; a 22 µH inductor joins it to VIN_DC.

pins.name: PAD
pins.function: Exposed thermal pad (PowerPAD), soldered to the board; the NC pins tie to it. It is not a power ground return.

circuits.title: Solar harvester with 80 % MPPT, 4.2 V storage limit and 1.8 V output
circuits.description: A solar cell feeds VIN_DC through CIN and L1 to the boost charger. VOC_SAMP is strapped to VSTOR, so the input is held at 80 % of the cell's open-circuit voltage, sampled onto CREF. The storage element on VBAT is charged up to VBAT_OV = 4.18 V (ROV1, ROV2); ROK1 to ROK3 put VBAT_OK at 2.39 V falling and 2.80 V rising; ROUT1 and ROUT2 set the buck output to 1.8 V for a load of up to 100 mA. operation.text: A boost charger draws µW to mW from a high-impedance DC harvester (solar cell, thermoelectric generator) into a storage element, and a nano-power buck turns the stored energy into a regulated rail. Once VSTOR is above VSTOR_CHGEN the main charger keeps working down to 100 mV on VIN_DC; from an empty VSTOR the cold-start circuit needs VIN(CS), 600 mV typical, to lift VSTOR to about 1.8 V. The buck is tuned for good efficiency from below 10 µA to about 110 mA.

The charger holds VIN_DC at a reference stored on CREF at VREF_SAMP, which sets the harvester's operating point. Every 16 s (typ) the charger stops for 256 ms (typ), lets VIN_DC rise to open circuit, and samples a fraction of it: 80 % with VOC_SAMP on VSTOR, 50 % with it on GND, or the ratio of ROC1 and ROC2. Solar cells usually peak near 70 % to 80 % of VOC, thermoelectric generators near 50 %. A microcontroller can instead supply the reference voltage itself.

VBAT_UV is fixed inside at 1.95 V typ falling, with VBAT_UV_HYST added for rising. Above VBAT_UV + VBAT_UV_HYST an internal PMOS switch joins VSTOR to VBAT; it opens again when VSTOR drops under VBAT_UV. The load belongs on VSTOR and the storage element on VBAT for this to protect the element. VBAT_UV is a last-resort limit; the load should be shed on VBAT_OK, set above it.

VBAT_OV is set with ROV1 and ROV2 and is also the level the charger regulates VSTOR and VBAT to when the input has power to spare. Above VBAT_OV the charger stops; it restarts after the battery falls by VBAT_OV_HYST, so with surplus input VBAT ripples between the two. If VSTOR sits at VBAT_OV while VIN_DC is above VSTOR, a low-resistance path shorts VIN_DC to ground; a source that can see this must have more than 20 Ω of impedance.

VBAT_OK reports whether VSTOR (and VBAT, while the PFET is on) is in a usable range, with a falling threshold from OK_PROG and a rising one from OK_HYST, independent of the OV and UV settings. Its high level is VSTOR and its low level ground; about 20 kΩ inside in series with the high side limits current into a microcontroller that is not yet powered.

Up the VSTOR scale: VSTOR_CHGEN (about 1.8 V, main charger runs if VIN_DC > 100 mV; below it cold start runs if VIN_DC > 600 mV), VBAT_UV and VBAT_UV + hysteresis (VBAT joined to or cut from VSTOR), VBAT_OK and VBAT_OK_HYST (load off or on), VBAT_OV − hysteresis and VBAT_OV (charging resumes or stops), and VSTOR's 5.5 V absolute maximum. Storage rises when harvested power times the converter efficiency exceeds the load, and falls otherwise.

The buck runs from VSTOR and regulates OUT to the ROUT1/ROUT2 setting with PFM control and internally sensed inductor current. It delivers up to 110 mA typical with a 200 mA inductor peak. It shuts off when VSTOR drops below VBAT_UV; between VBAT_UV and VOUT it runs at 100 % duty and passes VSTOR through.

Most of the internal circuitry runs at a low duty cycle, sampling and holding VSTOR. Every 64 ms VRDIV is switched on, first to VSTOR and then as the bias for the VBAT_OV and VBAT_OK dividers, which are compared with VBIAS; the divider current flows only during that brief window. Efficiency data were taken as an average of 50 input-current readings between MPPT samples, because both converters draw pulsed current.

There are five modes: cold start, ship mode (charger off), charger on, buck on, and thermal shutdown. Above VSTOR_CHGEN, EN and VOUT_EN choose among them. EN's high level is referred to VBAT and VOUT_EN's to VSTOR; EN not used goes to VSS. Cold start runs from VIN_DC; the main charger control runs from VSTOR while its power stage draws from VIN_DC.
EN high shuts the charger, the buck and the battery management down and opens the PFET between VBAT and VSTOR, the state with the least drain on the battery for long storage.

Cold start runs whenever VSTOR is under VSTOR_CHGEN while VIN_DC is at least VIN(CS) and input power exceeds PIN(CS): an unregulated hysteretic boost of lower efficiency charges VSTOR, with VIN_DC clamped to VIN(CS); EN and every other feature are inactive. Through the PFET's body diode it also has to charge the element on VBAT to about a diode drop below VSTOR_CHGEN. At VSTOR_CHGEN the IC sends an initialization pulse on VRDIV, stops the charger for 32 ms (typ) to capture the open-circuit voltage as the first MPPT reference, and takes its first feedback sample about 64 ms after the pulse. When the PFET then closes at VBAT_UV, the extra load can drop VSTOR back, so VSTOR may climb in steps while the IC cycles between cold start and the main charger. An external PFET between VSTOR and the load, driven by an inverted VBAT_OK, keeps the load off during this phase.

Discharge VSTOR before fitting a storage element with no source attached: if VSTOR is more than 100 mV above ground, the PFET stays off until a source appears. With VSTOR and VBAT both under 100 mV, attaching a charged element makes the IC close the PFET for tBAT_HOT_PLUG (45 ms) to bring VSTOR to VSTOR_CHGEN, open it, pulse VRDIV, pause the charger 32 ms for the MPPT reference, and sample feedback about 64 ms after the pulse. If VSTOR is still above VBAT_UV then, the PFET closes and charging starts; otherwise it stays open until the charger raises VSTOR to VBAT_UV. A load that pulls VSTOR down in the first 110 ms calls for the external load-isolating PFET.

Above VSTOR_CHGEN and with VIN_DC above 100 mV, the charger moves charge to VSTOR only while VIN_DC exceeds VREF_SAMP, using PFM. The inductor peak current steps through about 50 mA, about 100 mA and ICHG(CBC_LIM) as input current rises; in discontinuous mode up to 100 mA average input current is possible with a 230 mA typical peak. Charging stops at VBAT_OV, and the battery reaches VBAT_OV only if input power exceeds what the VSTOR load takes. The minor switching frequency depends on the inductor, the peak current limit and the voltages either side of it.

The buck is a hysteretic, peak-current, discontinuous-mode converter. Leaving ship mode (EN falling with VOUT_EN high) takes about 100 ms because the 64 ms sample-and-hold cycle must complete first. From standby (VOUT_EN rising) it starts much faster, in a time set by COUT, about 400 µs with 22 µF. It can start into a pre-biased output.

An on-chip sensor watches junction temperature; past the threshold the charger and buck stop and resume once it cools, with about 5 °C of hysteresis. The VBAT_UV switch still opens to protect the battery during shutdown. Ambient must stay within 85 °C; Li-ion cells need their own temperature protection from the application.

The storage element goes on VBAT and the load on VSTOR. Capacitors, supercapacitors and many battery types work; at least 100 µF equivalent capacitance is needed to absorb the charger's pulse currents. To charge CSTOR within tBAT_HOT_PLUG at hot plug, the element's series resistance plus the PFET's, times its equivalent capacitance, must be shorter than tBAT_HOT_PLUG. The element must carry the load through periods without harvest, and the harvester must refill it while the system sleeps.

Saturation current should be 25 % above the expected peak if load steps are expected. Both loops are hysteretic and so inherently stable. Boost: 22 µH ± 20 % between LBOOST (pin 20) and VIN_DC (pin 2), peak rating above 300 mA, low DCR. Buck: 10 µH ± 20 % between LBUCK (pin 16) and VOUT (pin 14), peak rating above 200 mA, low DCR; 4.7 µH is the floor, set by the peak-detect speed, and raises peak current and major frequency slightly.

Every capacitor should be low leakage. CREF holds the MPPT reference for about 16 s, so use X7R or C0G. CIN is at least 4.7 µF, scaled up for sources that look capacitive. VSTOR needs a 0.01 µF bypass close between VSTOR (pin 19) and VSS (pin 1) plus at least 4.7 µF of low ESR in parallel. VOUT takes at least 22 µF between pins 14 and 15; less capacitance means more ripple and droop. Large fast load steps or a high-resistance element can pull VSTOR under VBAT_UV or VSTOR_CHGEN; add CSTOR, or capacitance across the element if longer cold start is not acceptable.

Keep power traces wide and short and the capacitors and inductors close. Boost priority: the bypass (0.1 µF CBYP) and CSTOR between VSTOR (19) and VSS (1), then CIN between VIN_DC (2) and VSS (1), then L1 near LBOOST (20) and VIN_DC (2). Buck: COUT between VOUT (14) and VSS (15), L2 between LBUCK (16) and VOUT (14). Route inductors through vias and bottom traces rather than the capacitors. Keep divider midpoint traces to VBAT_OV, OK_PROG, OK_HYST and VOUT_SET short, and return the dividers and CREF on their own short traces to VSS pin 15; the PowerPAD is no power return. Use setting resistors above 1 MΩ for light-load efficiency, pour no ground near them or CREF, and clean boards well (rinse water above 50 MΩ), or cut the divider sum to at least 5× below the measured contamination resistance.
